items.followUp: What is Brownian motion, and what causes it?

rubric.why: Award for describing the irregular motion of particles suspended in a fluid.
rubric.description: Brownian motion is the random, irregular motion of particles suspended in a fluid.
rubric.how: State that the suspended particles move randomly or irregularly; an equivalent description is random zigzag motion.

rubric.why: Award for identifying collisions with fluid molecules as the cause.
rubric.description: It is caused by collisions of the fluid molecules with the suspended particles.
rubric.how: Explain that moving fluid molecules collide with and bombard the suspended particles.

modelAnswer: Brownian motion is the random, irregular motion of particles suspended in a fluid.
It is caused by collisions of the fluid molecules with these particles.

rubric.why: Award for the correctly normalized scientific notation of 0.00045.
Award for the correctly normalized scientific notation of 384000000.

items.followUp: Define a scalar quantity and give two examples.

rubric.why: Award for distinguishing vectors by their magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: State that a vector has both magnitude and direction.

rubric.why: Award for giving two valid vector examples.
rubric.how: Name any two vector quantities, such as force, velocity, displacement or acceleration.

modelAnswer: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.
Examples of vectors are force and velocity.

items.followUp: Define velocity and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Award for defining acceleration as the rate of change of velocity.
rubric.how: State that acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time.

rubric.why: Award for the correct SI unit.
rubric.description: State the SI unit of acceleration.
rubric.how: Give the unit as metre per second squared, m/s².

modelAnswer: Acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time.
Its SI unit is metre per second squared (m/s²).

items.followUp: State one difference between distance and displacement.

rubric.why: Award for a correct property of mass, preferably contrasted with weight.
rubric.description: State a distinguishing property of mass.
rubric.how: Mention that mass is the amount of matter in a body and is measured in kilograms.

rubric.why: Award for identifying weight as gravitational force and/or its unit.
rubric.description: State a distinguishing property of weight.
rubric.how: Mention that weight is the gravitational force on a body and is measured in newtons.

modelAnswer: Mass is the amount of matter in a body and is measured in kilograms (kg).
Weight is the gravitational force acting on a body and is measured in newtons (N).

items.followUp: A person pushes a wall. Identify the action and reaction forces and state which objects they act on.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the force exerted by the book on the table.
rubric.how: Explain that the book pushes the table downward.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the equal and opposite force exerted by the table on the book.
rubric.description: State the reaction force and its direction.
rubric.how: Explain that the table pushes the book upward; the two forces act on different bodies.

modelAnswer: The book pushes the table downward; this is the action force.
The table pushes the book upward with an equal and opposite force; this is the reaction force.
The action and reaction forces act on different bodies.

items.followUp: How does GPS help determine the position of a receiver on Earth?

rubric.why: Award for identifying GPS as a satellite-based positioning or navigation system.
rubric.how: State that GPS is the Global Positioning System, a satellite-based navigation system.

rubric.why: Award for explaining that satellite signals are used to find a location on Earth.
rubric.how: Explain that it uses signals from satellites to determine the position or location of a receiver on Earth.

modelAnswer: GPS (Global Positioning System) is a satellite-based navigation system.
It uses signals from satellites to determine the position of a receiver on Earth.

items.followUp: Resolve a force of 20 N acting at 30° to the positive X-axis into its rectangular components.

rubric.why: Award for the correct component along the X-axis.
Award for the correct component along the Y-axis.

modelAnswer: The component along the X-axis is Fₓ = F cos θ.
The component along the Y-axis is Fᵧ = F sin θ.
